outcome.descriptive: The two shell-write hooks agree on what a real copy lands: every file it wrote is one the plan gate graded before the command and one the bash-write guard attributes to it after.
outcome.technical: Written by the orchestrator (guard command-reading code). The finding asked for the same is_dir/files_of inputs in both hooks; that is not the structurally right answer, because guard-bash-writes runs AFTER the command (PostToolUse only) and the disk it could ask no longer says what it said before: `cp -r src/ lib/` that CREATED lib landed as lib/k.py, and a post-command disk reads the slash as inside an existing lib (lib/src). So the agreement is on the OUTCOME. guard-bash-writes._statement_targets now takes both landings the words allow - the shared reader's own reading and the one where no operand pre-existed (is_dir always False) - which costs nothing because it only names the statement that wrote a file already found changed, never a finding. New (ca) cases in test_guard_bash_writes run real copies in a scratch repo (cp a.py src, cp -r src/ lib/, mv a.py b.py out, cp a.py c.py) and require every landed file to be graded by guard-secrets-read._copy_targets beforehand AND named by writing_statement afterwards. ca2 was red before the change (named=[]) and passes after; 235/235. _config.copy_destinations' docstring no longer claims one command gets one answer - it says the two hooks read at two moments and the outcome is what agrees, held by (ca); the ww7c comment in test_guard_secrets_read is corrected the same way.
